message.reasoning_content:
Need to find Node.js 22 launch announcement (April 2024) about require() of native ES modules behind flag, and 22.12.0 release notes (Dec 2024) which enabled require(esm) by default without flag. The flag: --experimental-require-module. Disabling flag: --no-experimental-require-module. Error with top-level await: ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE. Runtime feature check: process.features.require_module.

Stability: Node 22.12.0 release notes said unflagging require(esm)... possibly "stabilized" — Node publish blog said feature was stabilized? Actually in Node 22.12.0 release, "require(esm) is now enabled by default by default" — the changelog for 22.12.0: "esm: unflag experimental-require-module" and mark as stable? The release notes: "This release includes an update to bring the Node.js 22.x line up... require(esm) enabled by default." Node 22.13/23... Actually Node 23 unflagged require(esm) earlier (23.0). For 22.12.0, changelog: "esm: enable require(esm) by default (Joyee Cheung)" semver-minor. Stability: not necessarily "stable" — enabling by default doesn't make it stable; it's still experimental? Node docs for v22.12: require(esm) — "Stability: 1.1 - Active development" maybe. Actually in Node 22 docs, require(esm) marked "Stability: 1.2 - Release candidate"? Let me check.

Launch announcement: Node 22 release blog (nodejs.org/en/blog/announcements/v22-release-announce) says require() of synchronous ES modules is behind --experimental-require-module flag.
